flawed_step: 0062: From f=(p-1)/2≤4, the proof incorrectly concludes that only p=5 remains. The prime p=7 also satisfies all these numerical restrictions.
counterexample: Take p=7. Then p is an odd prime greater than 3 and f=(p-1)/2=(7-1)/2=3. Thus f>1 and f≤4, exactly as required by the preceding argument, but p≠5. Hence the claim that f≤4 leaves only p=5 is false. (The p=7 case might be eliminated by an additional argument about x^3-z^3=2^σ, but no such argument appears before this conclusion.)
assessment_summary: Steps 0001–0061 are consistent with the stated results and preceding deductions. The first definite failure is the case enumeration in step 0062, which overlooks p=7.
